title: A Long-Term Study of Patient-Reported Changes in Depression, Anxiety, and Other Symptoms in People With Postpartum Depression (PPD) Starting Zuranolone
official: Evaluation of Symptom-Specific Improvements Following Treatment With Zuranolone: A Prospective, Observational Survey Study
summary:
In this study, researchers will learn how postpartum depression symptoms may change after people first start taking zuranolone. This is a drug available for doctors to prescribe for people with postpartum depression, also known as PPD. Research has shown that people who took zuranolone for PPD reported fewer depression symptoms. But, PPD can also affect anxiety, anger, and thinking skills. Researchers do not yet know how zuranolone affects these other symptoms in everyday life.

This is known as an "observational" study, which collects health information about study participants without changing their medical care. Participants for this study will be found in the United States using a database from Consumer Value Store (CVS) Specialty Pharmacy. This will include adults who filled a prescription for zuranolone through CVS Specialty Pharmacy between July 2026 and April 2027 and were within 12 months of the end of their pregnancy.

The main goal of this study is to learn more about how zuranolone affects the participants' depression and anxiety symptoms. This will be done using a survey about depression symptoms called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, also known as the EPDS. Researchers will also look at participants' anxiety using another survey called the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System, also known as the PROMIS.

The main question that researchers want to answer is:

• Do depression and anxiety symptoms change in participants with PPD after treatment with zuranolone based on EPDS and PROMIS scores measured at Day 15?

Researchers will also learn about:

• Changes in participants' anger, thinking skills, tiredness, and social skills based on PROMIS scores at Day 15 in the study

The study will be done as follows:

* People with PPD who fill their zuranolone prescription through CVS Specialty Pharmacy will be contacted by email or phone to ask them about their interest in participating in the study.
* Around the time they start taking zuranolone, participants will be asked to answer written questions about their symptoms using the online EPDS and PROMIS surveys. They will also answer other survey questions about their background, environment, and general health information.
* Participants will then be asked to answer questions using the EPDS and PROMIS surveys at 3 days, 15 days, 45 days, and 90 days after taking the first dose of zuranolone.
* All study activities will be done remotely using online surveys, email, text messages, or phone calls. Participants will be in this study for up to 90 days.
criteria:
Key Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults who were prescribed and had one successful fill for zuranolone within 12 months following the end of pregnancy for the treatment of PPD from July 2026 to April 2027 through CVS Specialty Pharmacy.
* Currently reside in the United States.
* Able to complete the questionnaires independently.

Key Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior fill of zuranolone or brexanolone in last 12 months.
* Taken more than one dose of zuranolone at the time of study screening.
* Current or history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder.
* Pregnancy that ended more than 12 months ago.

Note: Other protocol-defined Inclusion/Exclusion criteria may apply.
